threads.thread_goal: Align on current workflow, main pain points and pilot scope for one aisle.

messages.text: Hi team, let's kick off the backroom-to-shelf pilot. I'd like everyone to walk through how we currently move goods from the backroom to shelves. What are the main steps, where do handoffs happen, and what slows us down? Let's use this to map out A1 and identify the aisle and product categories we'll focus on for the pilot. Please share your perspective by EOD.

From the mover side, we get the truck in, unload pallets, check what's on the manifest, then move them to the backroom. We stack by aisle usually, but sometimes the backroom gets tight and we have to shuffle things around. Then shelf fillers come grab what they need. The issue is we don't always know which items are priority, so we might move something that's not needed yet.

On the shelf side, we grab stock from the backroom, bring it to the aisle, check the shelf life dates, rotate old stock to the front, fill gaps, and make sure prices are right. Sometimes the backroom is disorganised so we waste time hunting for items. And if something's damaged, we have to figure out what to do with it—there's no clear process.

I've been in most of these roles. The handoff between movers and shelf fillers is loose. Movers drop stock in the backroom, but shelf fillers don't always know when it arrived or what's priority. Also, we don't have a standard way to log damaged goods or missing items. Each person handles it differently. For the pilot, I'd suggest we focus on one aisle with high-rotation items—maybe the grocery section? That way we can test the process without disrupting too much.

Grocery makes sense. But we need to be clear on which product categories—canned goods, fresh, frozen? And when do we start? I can help map out the current workflow in A1 and draft the shift allocation in A6, but I'll need input from everyone on timing and exact scope.

Good points. Let's narrow it down: grocery aisle, canned goods and dry goods to start. That gives us a clear scope without overloading the team. For timing, we have 21 days total. I'd suggest we start the pilot on Monday of next week, run it for two full weeks, then spend the final week consolidating results. Does that work for everyone?
Monday works. I'll make sure the backroom is organised for the new sequence by then. But I need to know the exact loading order so I can plan the space. When will that be ready?
Monday is fine. I'm ready to test the new routine. Just need the checklist and the routine steps before we start.

The loading sequence will be ready by Friday. I'll coordinate with 36271 and 37492 to finalise it. 300804, can you have the workflow map A1 and shift plan A6 ready by Thursday? That way we can review everything together Friday before the pilot starts Monday.
I'll get A1 and A6 done by Thursday. I'll need to talk to each of you to fill in the details, so I'll send a quick form to everyone tomorrow to gather the info.
Sounds good. I can help with the loading sequence since I've done both roles. Let me know what you need from me.
Perfect. So to confirm: D1 is grocery aisle, canned and dry goods. D2 is start Monday next week, run for two weeks, wrap up week three. Everyone good with that?

threads.thread_goal: Define and validate the new loading, movement and shelf routines.

messages.text: Here's the first draft of the loading sequence A2 and the shelf routine A4. The loading sequence covers canned goods, dry goods, and a few high-rotation items. It's designed to minimise backroom congestion and make it easier for shelf fillers to grab what they need in order. The shelf routine includes rotation, shelf life checks, label changes, and price verification. Please review and flag any issues or concerns.

I looked at A2. The sequence makes sense for the first two categories, but I'm not sure about the weight distribution on the trolleys. If we stack canned goods too high, they'll be unstable when we move them. Can we add a note about max height and weight limits? Also, how do we handle items that need special care, like glass bottles?

Good catch. I'd add that canned goods can go higher because they're stable, but anything fragile should be on a separate trolley or lower on the stack. We should also note that the sequence assumes the backroom is organised by aisle, which it isn't always. Maybe we need a quick step in the sequence about how to organise the backroom first?

The shelf routine in A4 looks mostly good. But I have a question: what do we do if we find an item that's past its shelf life already on the shelf? Do we pull it immediately or note it for later? And how long should the rotation check take? I want to make sure I'm not spending too much time on one aisle.

If it's past shelf life, pull it immediately and log it in the incident log. For rotation, aim for 10-15 minutes per replenishment cycle. If you find something that takes longer, flag it so we can adjust. Let me update A2 and A4 with these notes and repost by tomorrow.
I also want to check: does the loading sequence in A2 account for cleaning? We need to make sure the backroom and aisles are clean before and after replenishment. Should that be part of T10?

Yes, cleaning is part of my routine. I usually clean the backroom at the start of the shift and after unloading. But if we're changing the loading sequence, I need to know when the best time to clean is so I don't block the shelf fillers.
Good point. Let's add to T10: cleaning happens before loading starts and after all stock is moved to the aisles. That way the backroom is clear for the next cycle. I'll add this to A2 as well.
One more thing: the sequence assumes we know what's coming on the truck. Can we add a step where the manifest is checked before unloading? That way we can plan the loading order in advance.

Absolutely. I'll add that to A2. So the updated sequence will be: check manifest, organise backroom, load by category, clean, then shelf fillers grab stock. Let me revise and post the final version by EOD tomorrow. Once everyone confirms it looks good, we can lock in D3.
Sounds good. I'm ready to test the routine once it's finalised.
I'll review the updated A2 and A4 tomorrow and confirm. Once we lock in D3 and D4, I can finalise the shift allocation in A6.
Perfect. Updated A2 and A4 are posted. Everyone, please confirm by EOD today so we can lock in D3 and D4 and move forward.
Confirmed. The updated sequence looks solid. I can work with this.
Confirmed. Ready to go.
Great. D3 and D4 are locked in. A2 and A4 are approved. 36271, 37492, 321832—you're all set for Monday. 300804, finalise A6 with the confirmed routines and share by Friday morning.

threads.thread_goal: Lock in safety, hygiene and incident logging practices for the pilot.

messages.text: Here's the draft safety and hygiene checklist A3 and the incident log template A7. The checklist covers lifting techniques, stacking safety, food hygiene, and cleaning. It's designed to fit on one page and be quick to use on shift. The incident log is simple: date, time, item, issue type, and action taken. Please review and let me know if anything is missing or unclear.

The checklist looks good, but I'd add a section on handling hazardous goods. We sometimes get items that need special care—cleaning products, for example. Also, the lifting section should mention when to ask for help if something's too heavy. I don't want anyone getting hurt.

For the shelf filler side, I'd add a check for shelf stability before filling. If a shelf is wobbly or damaged, we shouldn't load it. Also, what do we do if we find something damaged during replenishment? Do we log it immediately or finish the shelf first?

Good questions. If you find something damaged, log it immediately in A7 and set it aside. Don't continue filling until it's documented. I'll add the hazardous goods section and shelf stability check to A3.
The incident log is clear, but I'd suggest adding a 'resolved by' field so we know who fixed the issue. Also, should we have a daily summary of incidents, or just log them as they happen?

Good idea. I'll add 'resolved by' to A7. For the daily summary, let's log incidents as they happen, and I'll post a summary at the end of each shift. That way we catch issues quickly and can adjust if needed.
I can help with the daily summary. I'll check the incident log at the end of each shift and post a quick update to the channel. That way everyone knows what happened and what needs follow-up.

Perfect. So D6 is: log incidents as they happen in A7, and 300804 posts a daily summary at shift change. I'll update A3 with the hazardous goods and shelf stability sections, and A7 with the 'resolved by' field. Everyone, please confirm by EOD tomorrow so we can lock in D5.
Confirmed. The updated checklist will work for us.
Confirmed. I'm ready to use the checklist on Monday.
Excellent. D5 is locked in. Updated A3 and A7 are posted. Everyone review once more and confirm you're ready to use them starting Monday. T3, T9, and T12 are now ready to execute.

threads.thread_goal: Coordinate daily execution, tracking and quick fixes during the pilot.

messages.text: Pilot day one is here. Let's use this thread for daily updates. Please share: what was completed, any issues or delays, and what's planned for the next shift. I'll check the tracking sheet A5 and incident log A7 at the end of each day and post a summary. Let's keep it brief and actionable.

Day one morning shift: unloaded truck, organised backroom by category, loaded trolleys per A2. No major issues. Backroom is clean and ready for shelf fillers. One pallet of canned goods had a small dent, logged in A7. Ready for afternoon shift.

Day one afternoon shift: started replenishment on the grocery aisle. Followed A4 routine. Found three items past shelf life on the shelf—pulled them and logged in A7. Filled gaps and rotated stock. Took about 45 minutes for the full aisle. Shelf looks good. Will continue tomorrow.

I've been tracking the counts in A5. Day one numbers look good—no major discrepancies. I'll update the sheet at the end of each day. Also posted the incident summary: three items past shelf life, one dented pallet. All logged and resolved.

Great start, team. Day one is solid. 36271, the dented pallet—was it still usable or did we have to discard it? 321832, 45 minutes is good, but let's aim for 30-40 if possible. 300804, keep the tracking tight. We'll review the full week's data on Friday.
The dented pallet was still usable—just cosmetic damage. We used it. I'll try to speed up the loading tomorrow, but I need to make sure the trolleys are balanced. Can't rush safety.
I'll work on the timing. Some of the shelf life checks took longer than expected because the labels are small. But I'll get faster as I go.
Day two morning: truck arrived on time. 36271 and I coordinated the unload. Manifest was checked first per A2. Everything went smoothly. Backroom is organised and ready. No issues so far.
Day two afternoon: replenishment completed in 38 minutes. Better pace. Found one mislabeled item—price was wrong. Corrected it and logged in A7. Shelf looks full and clean.
Day two tracking: counts match the shelf. One mislabeled item caught and corrected. A5 is updated. Incident log shows one price error, resolved. Everything on track.

Excellent progress. Day two is even better than day one. 321832, 38 minutes is great. Keep that pace. 300804, the tracking is solid. Let's continue this rhythm through the week. Any blockers or concerns, flag them here immediately.
Day three morning: unloaded and organised. One item arrived damaged—logged in A7. Cleaned backroom after loading. Ready for shelf fillers.
Day three afternoon: replenishment done in 35 minutes. Routine is smooth now. No issues. Shelf is full and well-organised.
Day three: counts match. One damaged item logged. A5 updated. No discrepancies. Pilot is running smoothly.

Perfect. Three days in and the process is working well. Let's keep this momentum through the week. Friday we'll do a mid-pilot review to see if any adjustments are needed. Keep using A5 and A7 consistently.

threads.thread_goal: Review pilot results and agree on next steps and improvements.

messages.text: Pilot is complete. I've consolidated the results from A5 and A7 into A8. Here's the summary: stock accuracy was 98.5%, shelf presentation improved significantly, and we logged 12 incidents total—mostly minor (past shelf life items, one mislabeled price, one damaged pallet). The new process reduced replenishment time from 60 minutes to 35-40 minutes. Overall, the pilot was successful. Let's discuss what to keep, what to adjust, and whether to expand to other aisles.

The new loading sequence in A2 worked well. The backroom stayed organised and we didn't have any major safety issues. I'd keep the sequence as is. The only thing I'd suggest is adding a checklist for backroom organisation before we start loading—just to make sure everything is in the right place.

The shelf routine in A4 is solid. I got faster as I went, and the routine is now part of my normal flow. I'd keep it. The safety checklist A3 was helpful—I used it every shift and it kept me focused on the important stuff. No injuries or safety issues during the pilot.

The tracking sheet A5 and incident log A7 worked well. The daily summaries helped us catch issues quickly. I'd suggest we keep both and maybe add a weekly summary to track trends. For the next phase, we could expand to another aisle, but we'd need to make sure we have enough capacity.

The process is solid. The manifest check at the start of loading made a big difference—we knew exactly what was coming and could plan accordingly. I'd keep everything and expand to the next aisle. We have the routine down now, so it should be faster to implement elsewhere.

Good feedback. So the consensus is: keep the loading sequence A2, shelf routine A4, safety checklist A3, and tracking process A5 and A7. For improvements, add a backroom organisation checklist and a weekly trend summary. For expansion, we could move to the next aisle—maybe the frozen section? That would test the process on a different product type.
Frozen section makes sense. Different handling requirements, so it's a good test. I can adapt the loading sequence for frozen goods—they need different stacking and temperature considerations.
Frozen is good. The routine should be similar, but I'll need to check for freezer burn and make sure items are properly sealed. I'm ready to pilot that next.
I'll update A8 with the final recommendations and include the backroom checklist and weekly summary template. Once that's done, we can plan the next phase for the frozen section.

Perfect. D8 is locked in: keep the current process, expand to the frozen section, and add the backroom checklist and weekly summary. 300804, finalise A8 with all recommendations by EOD tomorrow. Then we'll schedule the frozen section pilot for next week. Great work, everyone. This pilot was a success.
Thanks for leading this. The process is solid and I'm confident we can scale it. Looking forward to the frozen section.
Great pilot. The routine is now second nature. Ready for the next phase.
